newsitem.title: INDIA: Mother Teresa calls for a family Christmas.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa calls for a family Christmas.

text.p: Mother Teresa, who returned home last week after heart surgery, on Monday sent out Christmas greetings to her admirers, asking them to build their families in dedication to God, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

"A family which prays together, stays together," the news agency quoted the 86-year-old Roman Catholic nun as saying in a Christmas message in Calcutta, from where she runs Missionaries of Charity, a religious order she founded.
"My prayer for you is that you make your family something beautiful for God," Mother Teresa said.
The Missionaries of Charity released in Calcutta an official message in which Mother Teresa said:

"My prayer for you is that when Christ comes to you in Christmas, He may find in you a warm home, warm love like that of a heartful of love, like that of a simple shepherd who was the first one chosen to see Christ."
The 1979 Nobel peace prize winner, known as the Saint of the Gutters for her devotion to the poor and dying, wished everyone love, peace, joy and unity, PTI said.
Mother Teresa spent three weeks in hospital in August and September for heart trouble, malaria and pneumonia. Two weeks later, she fell off a chair and hit her head.
She was admitted to hospital again in November to unblock two coronary arteries for the third such operation in five years.
Last week, Mother Teresa returned home after a long period of recovery delayed by bronchitis and irregular heartbeat
